title: Polyatomic Ions
description: Names, formulas, and charges for the 23 polyatomic ions in Table 2.5.

questions.answer: The -ate ion has one more oxygen than the -ite ion, and the charge is the same. "I ate more" (more oxygen).
per-…-ate has one more O than -ate; hypo-…-ite has one fewer O than -ite. ClO^- hypochlorite, ClO_2^- chlorite, ClO_3^- chlorate, ClO_4^- perchlorate, all 1−.
Each H^+ added raises the charge by one: PO_4^{3-} → HPO_4^{2-} → H_2PO_4^-. "Bi-" is an older word for hydrogen (bicarbonate = hydrogen carbonate).

questions.prompt: Nick the Camel ate a Clam for Supper in Phoenix
questions.answer: Consonants = number of oxygens, vowels = negative charge: NO_3^- nitrate, CO_3^{2-} carbonate, ClO_3^- chlorate, SO_4^{2-} sulfate, PO_4^{3-} phosphate.
-ide usually means a single-atom anion (Cl^- chloride), but hydroxide (OH^-), cyanide (CN^-) and peroxide (O_2^{2-}) are polyatomic ions that also end in -ide.
Ammonium. The "-ium" ending matches metal cations like sodium and potassium. Ammonium acts like an "honorary metal" and forms salts such as NH_4Cl.
Acetate. Acetic acid is vinegar. Picture a CH_3 "tail" stuck to a CO_2 "head" that carries the charge. You may also see it written C_2H_3O_2^-.
Cyanide. Cyanide is one of the three "-ide rebels" in this table, along with hydroxide and peroxide. "Cyan" comes from the blue pigment (Prussian blue) it was first made from.
Hypochlorite. "Hypo" means under, as in hypodermic (under the skin). Household bleach is sodium hypochlorite, NaClO.
Chlorite. Count up the chlorine ladder: hypochlorite 1 O, chlorite 2 O, chlorate 3 O, perchlorate 4 O.
Chlorate. It is the "Clam" in Nick the Camel ate a Clam…: 3 consonants (3 O), 1 vowel (1− charge).
Perchlorate. "Per" sounds like "super": the most oxygen. Perchlorate and permanganate are both per- ions with 4 oxygens and a 1− charge.
Dihydrogen phosphate. Each hydrogen cancels one negative charge: 3 − 2 = 1−.
Hydrogen carbonate (bicarbonate). Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO_3. In these names "bi-" means one hydrogen, not two.
Hydrogen sulfate (bisulfate). Same pattern as bicarbonate: "bi-" or "hydrogen" = one H added, charge goes up by one.
Hydroxide. Read it as "hydro + oxide." It is the ion in bases like NaOH, and another "-ide rebel."
Permanganate. It is shaped like perchlorate: XO_4^- with "per-" in front. Potassium permanganate, KMnO_4, is a deep purple solid.
Nitrite. "-ite" is always the lighter one: nitrite has fewer oxygens than nitrate. Nitrites are used to cure meats like bacon.
Nitrate. "Nick" in Nick the Camel…: 3 consonants (3 O), 1 vowel (1− charge).
Carbonate. "Camel" in Nick the Camel…: 3 consonants (3 O), 2 vowels (2− charge). Limestone and chalk are calcium carbonate, CaCO_3.
Chromate. Chromate is sulfate's twin: CrO_4^{2-} looks just like SO_4^{2-}. Swap S for Cr and you have it. Chromate compounds are often yellow.
Dichromate. Two chromates (Cr_2O_8^{4-}) minus one O^{2-} gives Cr_2O_7^{2-}. Dichromate compounds are bright orange.
Peroxide. Hydrogen peroxide is H_2O_2: two H^+ balance the O_2^{2-}. It is the third "-ide rebel."
Hydrogen phosphate. The phosphate staircase: PO_4^{3-} → HPO_4^{2-} → H_2PO_4^-. Each H added drops the charge by one step.
Sulfite. Learn sulfate first ("Supper"), then take away one O for sulfite. Sulfites are the preservatives listed on wine labels.
Sulfate. "Supper" in …a Clam for Supper…: 4 consonants (4 O), 2 vowels (2− charge).
Thiosulfate. "Thio" comes from the Greek word for sulfur. Think "sulfate with a sulfur swap."
Phosphate. "Phoenix" in …for Supper in Phoenix: 4 consonants (4 O), 3 vowels (3− charge).

questions.prompt: What is the name of NH_4^+?
questions.explanation: Ammonia is the neutral molecule NH_3. When it picks up an H^+, it becomes the NH_4^+ ion, ammonium. It is the only common polyatomic ion with a positive charge. Memory tip: The "-ium" ending matches metal cations like sodium and potassium. Ammonium acts like an "honorary metal" and forms salts such as NH_4Cl.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for acetate?
questions.explanation: Acetate is acetic acid (CH_3COOH) with its acidic H removed, leaving a 1− charge. CO_3^{2-} is carbonate and HCO_3^- is hydrogen carbonate. Memory tip: Acetic acid is vinegar. Picture a CH_3 "tail" stuck to a CO_2 "head" that carries the charge. You may also see it written C_2H_3O_2^-.

questions.prompt: What is the name of CN^-?
questions.explanation: CN^- is one carbon and one nitrogen with a 1− charge. Its name ends in -ide even though it has two atoms. Memory tip: Cyanide is one of the three "-ide rebels" in this table, along with hydroxide and peroxide. "Cyan" comes from the blue pigment (Prussian blue) it was first made from.

questions.prompt: What is the name of ClO^-?
questions.explanation: ClO^- has the fewest oxygens (one) in the chlorine family. The lowest one gets the "hypo-…-ite" name. Chloride is Cl^-, with no oxygen at all. Memory tip: "Hypo" means under, as in hypodermic (under the skin). Household bleach is sodium hypochlorite, NaClO.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for chlorite?
questions.explanation: Chlorite is the -ite form, so it has one fewer oxygen than chlorate (ClO_3^-). The charge stays 1−. Memory tip: Count up the chlorine ladder: hypochlorite 1 O, chlorite 2 O, chlorate 3 O, perchlorate 4 O.

questions.prompt: What is the name of ClO_3^-?
questions.explanation: ClO_3^- is the reference -ate ion for chlorine. The other three chlorine ions are named relative to it. Memory tip: It is the "Clam" in Nick the Camel ate a Clam…: 3 consonants (3 O), 1 vowel (1− charge).

questions.prompt: What is the formula for perchlorate?
questions.explanation: "Per-" means one more oxygen than the -ate ion. Chlorate is ClO_3^-, so perchlorate is ClO_4^-. Adding oxygen does not change the charge. Memory tip: "Per" sounds like "super": the most oxygen. Perchlorate and permanganate are both per- ions with 4 oxygens and a 1− charge.

questions.prompt: What is the name of H_2PO_4^-?
questions.explanation: Start from phosphate, PO_4^{3-}. Two H^+ ions raise the charge from 3− to 1−, and "di" names the two hydrogens. It still has 4 oxygens, so it stays "phosphate," not "phosphite." Memory tip: Each hydrogen cancels one negative charge: 3 − 2 = 1−.

questions.prompt: What is the name of HCO_3^-?
questions.explanation: Carbonate is CO_3^{2-}. Adding one H^+ lowers the charge to 1− and adds "hydrogen" to the name. It still has 3 oxygens, so it stays "carbonate." Memory tip: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate, NaHCO_3. In these names "bi-" means one hydrogen, not two.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for hydrogen sulfate (bisulfate)?
questions.explanation: Sulfate is SO_4^{2-}. One H^+ brings the charge to 1−. HSO_3^- would be hydrogen sulfite, and H_2SO_4 is neutral sulfuric acid. Memory tip: Same pattern as bicarbonate: "bi-" or "hydrogen" = one H added, charge goes up by one.

questions.prompt: What is the name of OH^-?
questions.explanation: OH^- is one oxygen and one hydrogen with a 1− charge. Oxide is O^{2-} alone, and hydride is H^- alone. Memory tip: Read it as "hydro + oxide." It is the ion in bases like NaOH, and another "-ide rebel."

questions.prompt: What is the name of MnO_4^-?
questions.explanation: MnO_4^- is the per- ion of manganese (Mn). Watch out: Mg is magnesium, a different element. Memory tip: It is shaped like perchlorate: XO_4^- with "per-" in front. Potassium permanganate, KMnO_4, is a deep purple solid.

questions.prompt: What is the name of NO_2^-?
questions.explanation: Nitrate is NO_3^-, so the ion with one fewer oxygen is nitrite. The charge stays 1−. Nitrogen dioxide (NO_2) is a neutral molecule with no charge. Memory tip: "-ite" is always the lighter one: nitrite has fewer oxygens than nitrate. Nitrites are used to cure meats like bacon.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for nitrate?
questions.explanation: Nitrate has 3 oxygens and a 1− charge. NO_2^- is nitrite, and N_3^- is azide. Memory tip: "Nick" in Nick the Camel…: 3 consonants (3 O), 1 vowel (1− charge).

questions.prompt: What is the name of CO_3^{2-}?
questions.explanation: CO_3^{2-} is the -ate ion of carbon, with 3 oxygens and a 2− charge. Hydrogen carbonate is HCO_3^-, with a 1− charge. Memory tip: "Camel" in Nick the Camel…: 3 consonants (3 O), 2 vowels (2− charge). Limestone and chalk are calcium carbonate, CaCO_3.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for chromate?
questions.explanation: Chromate has one chromium, 4 oxygens and a 2− charge. Cr_2O_7^{2-} is dichromate. Memory tip: Chromate is sulfate's twin: CrO_4^{2-} looks just like SO_4^{2-}. Swap S for Cr and you have it. Chromate compounds are often yellow.

questions.prompt: What is the name of Cr_2O_7^{2-}?
questions.explanation: "Di" means two chromium atoms. The charge is still 2−, the same as chromate. Memory tip: Two chromates (Cr_2O_8^{4-}) minus one O^{2-} gives Cr_2O_7^{2-}. Dichromate compounds are bright orange.

questions.prompt: What is the name of O_2^{2-}?
questions.explanation: O_2^{2-} is two oxygen atoms bonded together with a 2− charge overall. Oxide is a single O^{2-}. Superoxide is O_2^-, with only a 1− charge. Memory tip: Hydrogen peroxide is H_2O_2: two H^+ balance the O_2^{2-}. It is the third "-ide rebel."

questions.prompt: What is the name of HPO_4^{2-}?
questions.explanation: Phosphate (PO_4^{3-}) plus one H^+ gives HPO_4^{2-}. One hydrogen means no "di." It still has 4 oxygens, so it stays "phosphate." Memory tip: The phosphate staircase: PO_4^{3-} → HPO_4^{2-} → H_2PO_4^-. Each H added drops the charge by one step.

questions.prompt: What is the formula for sulfite?
questions.explanation: Sulfite is the -ite form, so it has one fewer oxygen than sulfate (SO_4^{2-}). The 2− charge does not change. Memory tip: Learn sulfate first ("Supper"), then take away one O for sulfite. Sulfites are the preservatives listed on wine labels.

questions.prompt: What is the name of SO_4^{2-}?
questions.explanation: SO_4^{2-} is the -ate ion of sulfur, with 4 oxygens and a 2− charge. Sulfide is S^{2-}, with no oxygen. Memory tip: "Supper" in …a Clam for Supper…: 4 consonants (4 O), 2 vowels (2− charge).

questions.prompt: What is the name of S_2O_3^{2-}?
questions.explanation: "Thio" means one oxygen has been replaced by a sulfur. Take sulfate (SO_4^{2-}), swap one O for S, and you get S_2O_3^{2-}. The charge stays 2−. Memory tip: "Thio" comes from the Greek word for sulfur. Think "sulfate with a sulfur swap."

questions.prompt: What is the name of PO_4^{3-}?
questions.explanation: PO_4^{3-} is the -ate ion of phosphorus, with 4 oxygens and a 3− charge. It is the only 3− ion in the table. Phosphide is P^{3-}, with no oxygen. Memory tip: "Phoenix" in …for Supper in Phoenix: 4 consonants (4 O), 3 vowels (3− charge).
